title: Characterization and Antioxidant Activity of Products Derived from Xylose–Bovine Casein Hydrolysate Maillard Reaction: Impact of Reaction Time

what_it_measured.text: Abstract: The characterization and antioxidant activity on Maillard reaction products (MRPs) derived from xylose and bovine casein hydrolysate (BCH) was investigated at 100 ◦ C and initial pH 8.0 as a function of reaction time.
Analysis of Fluorescence Properties The excitation and emission spectrum of xylose-BCH MRPs and BCH samples were determined through a F-4500 Fluorescence Spectrometer (Hitachi.

dose.text: Preparation of Bovine Casein Hydrolysate (BCH) Casein was dissolved in pH 7.4 phosphate buffer (0.04 mol/L) to an initial protein concentration of 75 g/L.

endpoint.text: Besides, the pH value of sample solutions was measured at 25 ◦ C. 2.4.
First, 20-µL samples (2.5 g/L) were injected, and their absorbances were measured at 214 nm.

reported_results.text: The 2,2-diphenyl-1-picryl-hydrazyl (DPPH) free radical scavenging capacity and ferrous reducing activity of xylose-BCH MRPs gradually increased with the reaction time extended from 0 to 8 h.
The pH values and free amino groups contents of xylose–BCH MRPs remarkably decreased with the reaction time up to 8 h, whereas their browning intensities significantly increased (p < 0.05).
The fluorescence property of xylose-BCH MRPs initially increased, and afterwards decreased with the reaction time extended up (p < 0.05).
However, the pH of xylose-BCH MRPs and heated xylose greatly decreased after the heat treatment of 8 h (p < 0.05).
The loss of free amino groups in heated BCH and xylose-BCH MRPs continuously decreased during the thermal treatment of 8 h (p < 0.05).
